'git status --porcelain' compares the worktree AND the index against HEAD; once the eight are in HEAD all three agree and the output is honestly empty. Its two guards against vacuity get STRONGER, not weaker: len(tracked)>=2 and the any-.md assertion now run against 40 files instead of 32. THE REAL DEFECT IS PRE-EXISTING AND STRUCTURAL, and the commit fixes only this instance of it: the test's own comment states its intent as 'the working tree agrees with the index', which is worktree-vs-index, but git status --porcelain is strictly broader and also reports index-vs-HEAD. Every future run that captures episodes will red this test in the window between git add and the commit. A narrower predicate that matches the stated intent is already GREEN right now, before any commit, and I ran both halves: 'git diff --name-only episodes/' is empty and 'git ls-files --others --exclude-standard episodes/' is empty. Recommended as a triage candidate, not a g4 fix.
